preview: Interview experience of Viraj Nerlekar for the Graduate Analyst role at Deutsche Bank, detailing 5 rigorous selection rounds including an online coding test, multiple technical rounds, a professional fitness round, and an HR round.
content: Deutsche Bank Interview Experience Viraj Nerlekar Final Year BTech IT Deutsche Bank visited our campus in the first week of August 2023 to hire Final year students for the role of Graduate Analyst. Their criteria was: • CPI : 7 and above • No criteria of 10th and 12th Percentage • Branches : Computer, IT & EXTC (Electronics and Telecommunication). There were 5 rounds conducted overall. • Online Coding Test. • Technical Round-1. • Technical Round-2. • Professional-fitness Round. • HR Round. You can refer to the coding questions and how many students were selected after each stage in the interview experience of others. Round 1 (HackerEarth Test ) (4th August, 2023. 5 pm) There were 3 coding questions with marks 20-40-40 sequentially. • Power Limit : I could only come up with a recursive approach and missed the last three test cases. • Auto Suggest : It was slight variation of standard edit distance question. We had to return string with minimum edit distance from the dictionary. Passed all test cases. • Backlink Sorting : This was pretty straight-forward did it by Pair class and Comparator for sorting. Passed all test cases. Online PPT (8th August, 2023) There was a Pre-Placement Talk on 8th August from 3pm to 4pm on MS Teams for the shortlisted candidates. Here, they introduced us to the organization structure, tech stacks, projects, values and details about the Deutsche Bank. 9th August, 2023 All the interviews were held offline in the TPO interview cabins. So we were supposed to reach TPO seminar hall at 8.30 am (though the actual interviews started around 10 am) in formals with 4 resume copies. Here I have tried to recollect maximum questions which were asked to me. Let’s Begin : Round 2 (Interview) (Technical Round-1) (~1hr) The interviewer didn’t ask me to introduce myself nor she introduced herself. She smiled, welcomed and greeted me and started asking questions. She asked me the following questions: 1) Explain OOPs in Java. 2) What did you do in your internship? What were your learnings from it? 3) How do you manage academics in VJTI? 4) Now she asked me to explain OOPs based on my Pizza Delivery Project (MERN). Like explain how you have used OOPs in your project on paper. Here I slightly struggled while devising an example for Polymorphism but later gave a good example and the interviewer seemed quite happy with it. 5) Then she asked me to create a table on paper. She told me the column names. Later she asked me to write following queries : • Write SQL query for creating the given table. • Write SQL query for inserting a record into the table. She also asked me how will I insert null values into the table. After writing these queries she told me to hand over the paper and she observed it carefully. • Some query involving GROUP BY and Count which I don’t remember exactly. • Write SQL query for finding customers who have made an order in the past month. Initially I struggled with this one. But later gave an approach of using MONTH(). • Write SQL query for finding customers who have made both veg and non-veg orders. 6) What are data structures? Explain them in brief. While explaining them she interrupted me and started asking : 7) Real life uses of stacks and queues. 8) Then she asked me to write code for implementing Queue using Stacks https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/queue-using-stacks/ on paper . Follow up questions : • How will you implement Stack using Queues? (Approach on paper) • How will you store other objects inside your Stack and Queues apart from Integers? (Java Generics). 9) Now comes the puzzle part. She gave me this puzzle : https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-chocolate-wrapper-puzzle/ I was not confident with the puzzle part as I had not practiced it. So when she told me the puzzle and I could not find the twist in it and directly gave a wrong answer. Then she told me that there is twist in it and I need to find it. It took me some time to find the twist and then later I reached the correct answer. Interviewer seemed quite happy after I reached the correct answer. (Meanwhile her coffee arrived and she asked me whether I want coffee ☕ too :)) Then she told me to write the code for the puzzle on paper and I did the same. Now comes the core part. She started flooding me with questions like : 10) What is DBMS ? 11) What is a flat file system? 12) One more question on flat file system which I could not recall. 13) What is a buffer manager? 14) What are different types of operating systems? 15) What is deadlock and how does it happen? 16) How can we prevent deadlocks? 17) What is a port? 18) What are sockets? Do you have experience with using sockets? She didn’t ask me if I had any questions for her. She told me that she is done with the interview and I will get the result for the 2nd round within few minutes. Round 3 (Interview) (Technical Round-2) (~1hr) The interviewer asked me to introduce myself. Then she asked why didn’t I take admission in Pune? Then that lead to a general conversation. Then in a while the interview began : 1) She asked me about my internship in detail. She also asked where did I exactly face difficulties during my internship and how I managed them. She asked some follow up questions on it. 2) Difference between Linux and Unix. 3) What operating systems you are familiar with? 4) Why people in VJTI prefer doing web development over app development the most? Is there any other domain apart from web development you are familiar with? 5) Then she asked me to explain my projects. Follow up questions : • State Management in React. • Why redux over context? I explained her how redux and redux-thunk work on paper and she seemed quite satisfied with the explanation. • Few questions on React and Java. 6) Then she asked me to name data structures I am familiar with. Then she told me that she will ask everything apart from these ☠. Then she gave me following two questions and told me to write code on paper: • Remove duplicate characters from given String. She told me not to use HashSet. Then we had short discussion on String and StringBuilder in Java. • Given a number like 232473183343. You have to sort all its digits and then return the number without using any sort. 7) Then she asked me whether I am familiar with Computer Networks. And then 8) What is an IP address? 9) What is a port? 10) Can we get exact location of someone from IP address? 11) Explain telnet command. (Thanks to CN LAB Vivas :)) 12) What is latency ? How will you reduce latency? 13) Is SQL a language? 14) Explain joins and their types on paper. 15) What is difference between Oracle Database and MongoDB? Why did you choose MongoDB? 16) What is difference between Git and GitHub. How you have used it? 17) What is CI/CD in GitHub? 18) Tell me something you are good at apart from your resume. 19) Later she gave me a complicated GitHub question. She described a scenario on paper, introducing some new keywords that I hadn't encountered before. I said I don't know the exact answer for the question but she told me to give it a try and answer whatever comes to your mind. I answered it and later she explained it to me. 20) Later she asked three situation-based questions. a) Suppose there is a project manager and he is consistently treating one individual in the team fairly while displaying unfair treatment towards rest of the team members. What are your thoughts on this situation? b) Now suppose the manager is exhibiting unfair treatment only towards a specific individual in the team. Thoughts on this? c) If you were that individual in both the situations, how would you manage being treated fairly on one hand, and unfairly on the other, by the manager? 21) At the end, she wanted me to provide an example of the situation she had discussed, considering both ethics and legality. I was able to give proper example. Then she asked If I had any questions for her, I asked about her life at DB. She explained me everything like how her day starts and wraps up at DB and the interview ended. Round 4 (Professional Fitness) (~40 mins) Firstly interviewer greeted me and asked me how was my day and overall interview process? Then he asked me whether I am feeling nervous? I told him that I am feeling excited as well as a bit nervous too. Then he laughed and told me that don't worry this might be the most easy round of all the other rounds . 1) He told me to introduce myself along with my family background. 2) What did you do in your internship? Did you work in a team during internship? 3) What negative test cases you handled inside the project (related to internship)? 4) Tell me about other test cases that you implemented. 5) Then he asked me whether I am interested in farming? Then he told me a story of someone, it was related to soil testing and asked me whether I would use soil testing in my farm and why? 6) Then he asked me questions like : 7) Why do you want to join DB? 8) What are your other goals in life apart from earning money? 9) How you will contribute to the society through DB? 10) Did you attend the PPT? Was everything fine during the PPT? 11) Explain something that you have apart from your resume. 12) Then he asked me to tell any DSA question that I had solved which relates to real life. (Told him stock buy and sell) https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock/ • Then he asked me whether I have used linked list in any of my project? • Then he asked whether I am familiar with tree traversals and then asked that can we do all traversals(DFS) in one traversal ? https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/preorder-postorder-and-inorder-traversal-of-a- binary-tree-using-a-single-stack/. He asked me to explain it on paper. He did not ask me to code it. 13) Then he started showing me a mobile application and told me that it is one of the 5000's of the products that DB has made. He kept explaining me the features inside the app and then he asked me how would I implement the pie chart feature in it? 14) He asked me did you face any language barrier after coming to Mumbai? 15) Then he started explaining me about life at DB and it led to some causal talks. During that I told him about the office of DB at CSMT and then he started telling the glory of that office. 16) Then he asked whether I am stuck at something or do I have flexibility? Then he explained how DB will give me flexibility. 17) He then asked whether I am encrypting the data stored inside MongoDB. He asked one question regarding the mongo connection string and data encryption. Later he explained me about TSL/SSL in MongoDB and told me to do a search about it. Then he asked if I have any questions and I asked him two(one regarding the work culture and other regarding the new joiners) and the interview ended. Round 5 (HR) (15-20 mins): I was surprised to see two interviewers during my HR round. Initially I was confused a little bit but later I managed it . The interviewers were quite friendly. 1) Introduce yourself. 2) How was your experience until now? 3) What did you do in your internship and what were your learnings from internship? a. While explaining the learnings they both asked some follow up questions. 4) Suppose you have made a design A and group of people in the same team have made design B. You think your design is better and they think their design is better. Then how will you handle this situation and tell that your design is better? 5) Then they asked me, during your internship whether a situation arose where the implemented solution was satisfactory but a more efficient alternative was available, and how did I handle that particular situation. 6) Then there was a scenario-based question. One interviewer explained it to me. The other interviewer also explained it but in a different manner. Finally, I gave an answer, and they both started laughing. Then again, they both explained the situation, and I gave the proper answer. 7) Then they asked questions like why DB, and the interview ended. Even though I was tired I really enjoyed the last interview. The interviews concluded around 8 PM and we got the results within an hour. 26 candidates were selected and I was happy to be one among them . RESOURCES: • DSA : StriverAtoZ, Leetcode, GFG. • OS : Gate Smashers, Love Babbar, GFG. • DBMS : Gate Smashers, Love Babbar, GFG. • SQL : GFG, Love Babbar, Edureka, Leetcode. • CN : Love Babbar. • Core Java : Abdul Bari(Udemy), Durga. • System Design : Gaurav Sen, Soumyajit Bhattacharyay, Shreyansh Jain. TIPS: ● Start as early as possible. I myself started preparing very late i.e. in the end of the 2nd year. Remember the earlier you start, the more time you have to work on your skills and develop confidence. Being consistent is very important. ● Do not lie on your resume. Remember, you may lie, but your eyes will not lie to the interviewer. Prepare all the things (each and every word) that is there on your resume because the interviewer expects you to know everything that is present on your resume. ● Don’t compare yourselves with others. It is waste of time because everyone has gone through different phase during preparation. Know your strengths and weaknesses and start working upon them. Sometimes you may realize that there is randomness (somewhat) in the selection process but we have to accept that we can’t do anything for the things which are not in our hands. ● Knowing a thing is different and being able to explain it to others is a different thing. Do refer GFG archives and Past year COC interview experiences. ● All study and not getting shortlisted makes Jack a dull boy. Total questions solved, Submission time, CGPA, Plagiarism and CV might affect the shortlisting. So keep all these factors in mind. ● Prepare Data Structures and other core subjects thoroughly. As you prepare, also think about how you'd explain the topic or problem (brute ->better -> optimal solution) to the interviewer if they ask you the same. ● Instead of doing lots of things, focus on doing the things that truly matter and do them thoroughly. ● If you are ignoring HR questions then you might be doomed. Prepare them well too. ● You can practice giving mock interviews with your friends and try to improve yourself. That will be very beneficial. ● Stay healthy. Stay Calm. Stay Confident and Keep Fighting until you chase your dreams. All the Best !!! Feel free to ask anything : Email LinkedIn
